take_homes: The test for whether this is real: ask the agent a hard question and check that every claim cites a file I gave it. I can run that myself.
The assets here are plain text files I own, which survive a change of model or vendor. That's a lot less lock-in than the last programmes.
The agent is only as good as what we have written down, and most of what matters in our company isn't written down.

monday.move: Take one live decision (a partner or vendor question) and build a small memory with 5 to 8 sources. Ask it one hard question and see if it cites properly.
monday.who: Me, alone. I tell nobody until I know whether it works.
monday.when: One evening next week, 45 to 60 minutes. Not Monday.
monday.stop_condition: If after adding one new source the pages are just longer and the answers are still generic, I drop it.
monday.blocker: The steering group calendar, and whether the data policy lets me put the vendor material in.

misconception.why: The old line was that this would blow over like agile and OKRs. Here I get a test I can run myself: add a source and check whether the pages get sharper, and whether answers cite my files. The folder also survives the model changing, so it doesn't look like another fad. I haven't run it, and 'keeps getting better' is still a claim until I do.

one_line: Less hot air than I expected. The test where every claim must cite my own files is real, but I'll believe the compounding after a week of use.
